reflection.text:
I anchored on the two acquired wells: 10 uM (e2: frac_large_nucleus z=+23.0, act_glcm_contrast z=+21.7, tub_mean z=+11.9) and 1 uM (e3: act_glcm_contrast z=+9.8, frac_large_nucleus z=+8.7 persisting), and read persistence of actin texture plus large/multinucleate signal as primary Actin disruption. The second describe_phenotype on the 1uM well (e11) naming Actin disruptors reinforced that despite low density in both looks.

The review critique was correct: I overcalled a plurality. Compare_to_reference_atlas (e5) favored Protein synthesis (4/10, top neighbour) over Actin disruptors (3/10), and the first microscopist (e4) proposed Microtubule stabilizers/Aurora kinase inhibitors, not Actin. The attempted dose_responses (e6-e8) were invalid with only 2 single-replicate wells, and high actin/tubulin brightness at 10 uM could be secondary to mitotic rounding and density loss rather than direct actin biology.

I missed Epithelial entirely because it was never in the hypothesis set (e9, e12) and my acquisition choice used the whole 2-well budget on high/mid doses (10 uM and 1 uM) with no low-dose or replicate titration to test junctional spreading versus cytokinesis failure. Without epithelial markers or shape-context quantitation, I mistook a strong secondary cytoskeletal texture for mechanism.
what_was_right: Recognized that act_glcm_contrast and frac_large_nucleus persisted from 10 uM (e2) to 1 uM (e3), arguing against a pure high-dose toxicity artifact.
Kept uncertainty explicit with low probabilities (0.45 then 0.38) and retained Protein synthesis, Microtubule stabilizers, Aurora and Eg5 alternatives (e9, e12) given the split atlas (e5).
Used the free follow-up describe_phenotype on the 1 uM well (e11) as requested to test whether actin signal persisted without strong mitotic confound.
what_was_wrong: Submitted Actin disruptors despite e5 favoring Protein synthesis (4/10) over Actin (3/10) and e4 favoring Microtubule stabilizers/Aurora, making p=0.45 uncalibrated as the review noted.
Treated two single-replicate wells as dose support when e6-e8 explicitly stated need for at least 3 wells over 2 concentrations for a trend.
Overweighted act_glcm_contrast z=+21.7/+9.8 and tub_mean z=+11.9/+5.9 (e2/e3) while underweighting mitotic-rounding/density-loss confounds and the e5 protein-synthesis lead.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Top call not favoured: atlas leads Protein synthesis (4/10, top neighbour, mean sim 0.785) over Actin (3/10, 0.765); phenotype report candidates were Microtubule stabilizers/Aurora, not Actin. High act/tub brightness and act_glcm_contrast could be secondary to mitotic rounding at 10µM (frac_mitotic_like z=+5.0), and 'dose response' has only 2 single-replicate wells (invalid trend per e6-e8). p=0.45 is therefore uncalibrated plurality.

## Reflection

I anchored on the two acquired wells: 10 uM (e2: frac_large_nucleus z=+23.0, act_glcm_contrast z=+21.7, tub_mean z=+11.9) and 1 uM (e3: act_glcm_contrast z=+9.8, frac_large_nucleus z=+8.7 persisting), and read persistence of actin texture plus large/multinucleate signal as primary Actin disruption. The second describe_phenotype on the 1uM well (e11) naming Actin disruptors reinforced that despite low density in both looks.

The review critique was correct: I overcalled a plurality. Compare_to_reference_atlas (e5) favored Protein synthesis (4/10, top neighbour) over Actin disruptors (3/10), and the first microscopist (e4) proposed Microtubule stabilizers/Aurora kinase inhibitors, not Actin. The attempted dose_responses (e6-e8) were invalid with only 2 single-replicate wells, and high actin/tubulin brightness at 10 uM could be secondary to mitotic rounding and density loss rather than direct actin biology.

I missed Epithelial entirely because it was never in the hypothesis set (e9, e12) and my acquisition choice used the whole 2-well budget on high/mid doses (10 uM and 1 uM) with no low-dose or replicate titration to test junctional spreading versus cytokinesis failure. Without epithelial markers or shape-context quantitation, I mistook a strong secondary cytoskeletal texture for mechanism.

What was right:
- Recognized that act_glcm_contrast and frac_large_nucleus persisted from 10 uM (e2) to 1 uM (e3), arguing against a pure high-dose toxicity artifact.
- Kept uncertainty explicit with low probabilities (0.45 then 0.38) and retained Protein synthesis, Microtubule stabilizers, Aurora and Eg5 alternatives (e9, e12) given the split atlas (e5).
- Used the free follow-up describe_phenotype on the 1 uM well (e11) as requested to test whether actin signal persisted without strong mitotic confound.

What was wrong or missed:
- Submitted Actin disruptors despite e5 favoring Protein synthesis (4/10) over Actin (3/10) and e4 favoring Microtubule stabilizers/Aurora, making p=0.45 uncalibrated as the review noted.
- Treated two single-replicate wells as dose support when e6-e8 explicitly stated need for at least 3 wells over 2 concentrations for a trend.
- Overweighted act_glcm_contrast z=+21.7/+9.8 and tub_mean z=+11.9/+5.9 (e2/e3) while underweighting mitotic-rounding/density-loss confounds and the e5 protein-synthesis lead.
- Never hypothesized or tested Epithelial: spent the 2-well budget on 10 uM and 1 uM only, with no titration for junctional/epithelial morphology and no compound lookup value (e14 no structure/mechanism).

Proposed next experiment: Full 0.01-30 uM titration in replicate with DNA + F-actin + microtubule + E-cadherin/keratin and phospho-H3, scoring cell density, cell-cell junctions and spreading vs binucleate/cytokinesis-failure rate and actin foci/loss of stress fibers, plus washout to distinguish primary actin disruption from epithelial differentiation/junctional remodeling.
